summary_for_principal:
Processes can now run several tracks of work side by side — checking a proposal from three angles at once, say — continuing only once every track finishes, per a rule the author picks (all must succeed, any one is enough, or just that all finished regardless).

While building this I found and closed a real security gap the design would otherwise have introduced: an approval step after this parallel work could, in one layout, end up approving work it had just done itself — the exact self-approval this format exists to prevent. Fixed before shipping, not merely noted.

I also read one design-spec sentence as ambiguous — whether a decision can be reached the moment it's certain, before every track finishes — and chose the safer reading: always wait for every track, since nothing here can yet abandon work partway through. Flagged for the spec to state this explicitly.

Full test suite: 459 passed. Lint, formatting and type checks all clean.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding — built, tested, ready to merge when green.
2. First of three planned parts for parallel work. Next: iterating over lists of items the same way.

also.reason: Five new tests: A1 (all-success join), A2 (an early branch failure does not short-circuit the join), A3 (ANY_SUCCESS does not short-circuit on the first success), A6 (a branch's own process call hits the same depth limit an un-nested call would), and a regression proving a branch-produced value cannot be self-reviewed by a GATE reached after the join.
D46 added to §18; §7.4 gains the engine-executed operational paragraph; §9.2 notes a branch shares its parent's depth; §12.1/§12.2 note PARALLEL/JOIN dispatch and the join's own audit record.

Part 1's own design (reuse _drive_scope for a branch, evaluate policy against each branch's own outcome, A1-A3/A6 acceptance criteria) is what this PR implements — except for the branch/parent state relationship and the join's own early-exit question, both left unstated there and resolved here (see D46's own filled_in gaps below).

interpretation.read_as: Implement WP-03 Part 1 (PARALLEL + JOIN, acceptance criteria A1-A3 and A6) largely as designed, resolving two genuine gaps the design document itself left open rather than guessing silently: how a branch's own state relates to the parent's (one shared, process-wide namespace, per spec §2.2 and the absence of §7.5's own explicit "isolated" wording for PARALLEL), and whether the join can short-circuit once its policy is already decidable before every branch finishes (no — this engine has no cancellation primitive for a still-open branch).

filled_in.gap: The design document says a branch is driven through _drive_scope "the same shape one level down" as a PROCESS call's own child, but does not say whether a branch's own state is isolated (like a FOR_EACH item's, spec §7.5) or shared with the parent and its sibling branches.
filled_in.assumed: One shared, process-wide state namespace (spec §2.2 declares exactly one), seeded into each branch from the parent's current state and threaded sequentially branch-to-branch, then folded back into the parent once every branch ends. This is the only reading consistent with §7.4's own "two branches writing one REPLACE channel is refused" sentence, which is only a meaningful risk under a SHARED namespace — an isolated one could never have two branches contending for the same channel at all.
filled_in.grounded_in: Spec §2.2's single state.<channel> namespace, cross-checked against §7.4's own REPLACE-conflict sentence and §7.5's explicit isolation language (present for FOR_EACH, absent for PARALLEL) as textual evidence the difference is deliberate.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Medium — switching to isolated branch state later would need a new merge-back rule for whatever a branch's own output should still reach the parent with (this pass's threading approach reuses zero new machinery, an isolation model would need to invent some).

filled_in.gap: Spec §7.4 says "the join runs exactly once, when its policy is met or can no longer be [met]" — read literally, this could license an early exit the moment a policy's outcome is already decidable (e.g. ANY_SUCCESS satisfied by the first branch to succeed, while two remain open).
filled_in.assumed: Never short-circuit — always wait for every branch to reach its own ending before evaluating the join, regardless of whether the policy's answer is already knowable sooner. This engine has no primitive to cancel a still-open branch's own pending hand-off; an early exit would either abandon that branch's scope permanently unresolved (breaking §12.2's own write-once-per-node promise) or require inventing a new cancellation primitive this pass does not build.
filled_in.grounded_in: CLAUDE.md's 'refuse rather than guess' precedent (D26/D34/D38/D45) applied to a genuinely ambiguous spec sentence — chose the reading buildable from what already exists rather than inventing a new primitive to support the other reading.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Low — an early-exit optimisation is additive on top of this pass's own "wait for all" baseline, addable later once a cancellation primitive exists, without changing anything this pass built.

decisions.headline: D46 — PARALLEL/JOIN are now dispatched by the engine: a branch is a nested scope sharing the parent's node map and process-wide state, terminating via an ordinary declared ending; the join always waits for every branch; a latent self-review bypass this shape would otherwise reopen is closed by threading produced_by provenance out of a branch.
decisions.problem: The design document's own reuse-_drive_scope approach left two things unstated (branch/parent state relationship, whether the join can short-circuit) and, while implementing the shared-state design those gaps forced, a third, more serious issue surfaced unprompted: a GATE's own 'no deciding on your own work' check (§7.6) depends on produced_by, a purely local dict inside _drive_scope's own call — never returned, so a value a BRANCH's own step wrote would be invisible to a GATE reached after the join, silently defeating that separation-of-duty control for exactly the case PARALLEL makes newly reachable.
options_rejected: Isolate branch state entirely, each branch getting its own private state dict never folded back: rejected — contradicts spec §2.2's single-namespace model directly and would make the spec's own §7.4 worked example (a join feeding a step that reads what each lens branch computed) impossible to express.

Ship the produced_by gap as a documented, accepted limitation (the same treatment D45 gave the inherited backoff-sleep gap): rejected — that precedent fits a minor, bounded operational nuance; this gap is a security-relevant control silently regressing for a genuinely reachable, easily-authored shape, precisely the 'bad-but-conformant attack' CLAUDE.md's own principles ask this format to survive rather than narrate.

Let _advance_join short-circuit once its policy is already decidable: rejected — no primitive exists in this engine to cleanly abandon a still-open branch's own pending hand-off; building one is a materially bigger, separately-scoped feature.
decisions.cost_to_change: Low — every new field (_DriveResult.produced_by, _Advance.produced_by, _drive_scope's three new keyword parameters) is additive with a default preserving prior behaviour at every existing call site; _advance_parallel/_advance_join/_drive_parallel_branches are reached only for PARALLEL/JOIN nodes.

lessons.maxim: A shared-state design's own second-order effects (here: provenance tracking, not just the state values themselves) need the same threading discipline as the primary value being threaded — checking only 'does the state value survive' misses a control that depends on WHO wrote it, not just what was written.
lessons.incident: Seeding and folding a PARALLEL branch's own state writes back into the parent was the obvious, necessary fix for branch reads/writes to work at all; produced_by (the identity that wrote each path) is a SEPARATE piece of bookkeeping _drive_scope already builds for STEPs, and it would have been silently dropped at exactly the same fold-back point had this pass not traced through what a GATE's own self-review check actually depends on before considering the state-threading work complete.
lessons.destination: CLAUDE.md's 'Survive the bad-but-conformant attack' principle — this incident is a concrete instance of that principle catching a real gap during design, worth citing as precedent the next time a new execution shape threads state through an existing security-relevant check.
